title: Setting Up ImGui with Win32 and DirectX 11
summary: Dear ImGui is a handful of source files you add to your project, plus a **platform back end** (input and windows) and a **renderer back end** (drawing). This lesson builds the standard Win32 + DirectX 11 program step by step, the same set-up as ImGui's own example.
ideas:
- Build `examples/example_win32_directx11` from the ImGui repository and run it.
- Then create your own empty Win32 project, add the files from the table, and reproduce the example from scratch with the code above.

cards.q: Which files make up a typical Win32 + DirectX 11 ImGui set-up?
cards.a:
The ImGui core .cpp and .h files plus imgui_impl_win32 and imgui_impl_dx11 from the backends folder

You compile the core files into your program and add one platform back end (Win32) and one renderer back end (DX11) from backends/.

cards.q: List the calls at the start and end of every frame.
cards.a:
Both back ends' NewFrame, then ImGui::NewFrame; ImGui::Render, then the DX11 RenderDrawData

Start with ImGui_ImplDX11_NewFrame, ImGui_ImplWin32_NewFrame and ImGui::NewFrame; end with ImGui::Render and ImGui_ImplDX11_RenderDrawData(ImGui::GetDrawData()). Render only builds the draw data; the renderer back end draws it.

cards.q: In what order do you shut ImGui down?
cards.a:
The renderer back end, the platform back end, then DestroyContext: the reverse of setting up

Shut down in the reverse order of setting up, so nothing uses the context after it is gone.

cards.q: What does the renderer back end do?
cards.a:
Draws ImGui's triangles and textures with your graphics API

The platform back end handles input and the window; the renderer back end draws.

At the start of your window procedure, so ImGui sees input first

It turns every window message into ImGui input, so it must see each message as it arrives.

cards.q: When should a game draw ImGui?
cards.a:
After its own scene, so the interface appears on top

ImGui's draw data is rendered over the finished frame, just before Present.
